newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-ZANARDI EARNS CLEVELAND POLE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ZANARDI EARNS CLEVELAND POLE.

text.p: Italy's Alessandro Zanardi cemented his third CART pole this year amd 10th overall Saturday with an intimidating lap in the closing seconds of qualifying for Sunday's Cleveland Grand Prix.

Zanardi, driving a Reynard Honda, won the provisional pole on Friday, then failed to improve his time around the 10-turn, Burke Lakefront Airport until the final lap when he tore off a record lap of 56.984 seconds for an average speed of 133.048 mph (14.114 kph), more than a half of a second faster than the similar car of Brazilian Gil de Ferran.

Third fastest and coming off his win at the last race, at Portland, Oregon, was Briton Mark Blundell in a Reynard Mercedes-Benz at 57.538. Michael Andretti, winner of the opening round at Homestead was fourth at 57.637 seconds in a Swift Ford.

Watching his rivals improve their times but fail to surpass his, Zanardi said his team wasn't certain of holding onto the pole. "We knew if we wanted to stay on pole we would have to go a little faster".

He knew his car was still faster than his competition but his problem was getting around the slower cars. "It was a matter of getting a clear lap, which wasn't until the last lap. I was lucky to cross the start finish line with one second left (in the session) and there was no one in front of me," said Zanardi.

DeFerran, last year's winner here, wasn't worried about the big difference between his time and Zanardi's. "It's been a tough weekend. The car's been nervous. We made some changes and the car was greatly improved," he said.
Twenty-eight drivers are scheduled to start the 90-lap race on Sunday, the tenth event in the 17 race series.
